exact_statement: For any finite d-bit Boolean sign g, let E contain all coordinate parity vectors, m(v)=min(P(v dot S=1),1-P(v dot S=1)), r_E(t)=rank_F2{v in E:m(v)<=t}, N(t)=#{j:m(e_j)<=t}, and chi=sum_j(2Inf_j(g)-1)_+. Its minimum influence a_E over parity bases from E and translations equals integral_0^(1/2)(d-r_E(t))dt, and the actual affine release equals chi+integral_0^(1/2)(r_E(t)-N(t))dt. This supplies a full-release lower bound and spends overlapping parity gains only once. For every integer k>=2,p=2^-k, Q=(-1)^(ab+ac+bc+za), F_k=1-A_k+A_k Q, the original proper pair(a,b) has I_A=p, exact full affine child release rho_A=p/4 and zero character-only child release. Its complete decrement L_A satisfies (15/4)p<L_A<(595/128)p, so after the explicit one-branch parity reset it is paid at SAME K=15/4 with margin>5p/128. The same query/reset/payment holds after tensoring ANY disjoint Boolean core left untouched in every terminal. The three nonconstant optimized terminals violate K=15/4 for k>=16, so no terminal nonviolation or full FEI follows.
